cases.statement: One Chinese family (PMID 30714332): affected proband III-1 (male, 18), his younger brother III-2 (male, 13) and their mother II-2 (female) carry the variant; the father II-1 does not. Zygosity words are not used; the paper calls them carriers.

people.label: III‐1
people.key_phenotypes: cardiomyopathy diagnosed at 3; ventricular pre-excitation and complete LBBB; biventricular hypertrophy with LVEF 30% and reduced myocardial T1; CK 3778 U/L and raised transaminases with myogenic EMG; autophagic vacuoles with sarcolemmal features on muscle biopsy; average intelligence

quotes.quote: The proband was an 18‐year‐old male. At the age of 3 years, the patient was diagnosed with cardiomyopathy and his physical development was somewhat delayed from an early age (Figure 1a).
Electrocardiogram revealed frequent atrial premature beats, ventricular pre‐excitation, complete left bundle branch block, and double ventricular hypertrophy.
creatine kinase (CK), 3778 U/L (38–174 U/L)

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the patient revealed left and right ventricular wall hypertrophy, accompanied by a decrease in overall contractile activity, left atrioventricular enlargement, and decreased myocardial T1 value (Figure 1b,c).

Pathological analysis revealed numerous vacuoles in the myocytes, positive periodic acid‐Schiff (PAS) staining in the vacuoles, and positive staining of the vacuolar edge membrane protein, indicating myogenic damage and autophagic vacuoles with sarcolemmal features (AVSF).
His intelligence is average, and he can complete everyday tasks and simple calculations.

Sanger sequencing verifying that the proband (III‐1) and his mother (II‐2) and younger brother (III‐2) carried the mutation in LAMP2, c.741+1G>T. The patient's father (II‐1) did not carry the mutation.

people.label: III‐2
people.key_phenotypes: age 13; ST-T changes and ventricular pre-excitation; non-uniform myocardial echo with normal contraction; CK 2217 U/L, raised LDH and transaminases; no limb muscle abnormality

quotes.quote: The patient's younger brother (III‐2; 13 years old) showed an ST‐T change in electrocardiogram and ventricular pre‐excitation.
Blood analysis showed liver and muscle enzyme abnormalities, CK, 2,217 U/L; lactate dehydrogenase, 1,155 U/L (109–245 U/L); ALT, 307 U/L; and AST, 377 U/L.
There was no obvious abnormality in the limb muscles, nor was there atrophy of the skeletal muscle.

Sanger sequencing verifying that the proband (III‐1) and his mother (II‐2) and younger brother (III‐2) carried the mutation in LAMP2, c.741+1G>T. The patient's father (II‐1) did not carry the mutation.

people.label: II‐2
people.zygosity_or_genotype: carrier (female; zygosity not stated); mother of III-1 and III-2
people.key_phenotypes: slightly enlarged left atrium and ventricle with preserved systolic function; atrial fibrillation

quotes.quote: The mother of the proband (II‐2) had a slightly enlarged left atrium and left ventricle, with no obvious abnormalities in left ventricular systolic function. The electrocardiogram waveform indicated atrial fibrillation.

Sanger sequencing verifying that the proband (III‐1) and his mother (II‐2) and younger brother (III‐2) carried the mutation in LAMP2, c.741+1G>T. The patient's father (II‐1) did not carry the mutation.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Proband: cardiomyopathy with pre-excitation, high CK and vacuolar myopathy, which the authors call characteristic. Whole-exome sequencing was done; the paper does not state findings in other genes. The authors note reduced T1 separates metabolic cardiomyopathy from classical HCM.

quotes.quote: By whole exome sequencing analysis, we identified a novel pathogenic mutation in LAMP2 c.741+1G>T.
In this patient, the T1 value of the heart was reduced, strongly indicating metabolic cardiomyopathy.
Finally, we diagnosed the patients with Danon disease, based on their medical history, genetic test results, and family history.

segregation.statement: Three carriers in two generations (mother II-2, sons III-1 and III-2), all with cardiac findings; the father II-1 does not carry it and has normal ECG and echocardiography.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing verifying that the proband (III‐1) and his mother (II‐2) and younger brother (III‐2) carried the mutation in LAMP2, c.741+1G>T. The patient's father (II‐1) did not carry the mutation.
The patient's father (II‐1) had normal electrocardiogram and echocardiography (Figure 2).
Sanger sequencing confirmed that the proband, his mother, and his brother are carriers of this mutation.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the sons: inherited from the carrier mother. The mother's own parents are not reported as tested.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing verifying that the proband (III‐1) and his mother (II‐2) and younger brother (III‐2) carried the mutation in LAMP2, c.741+1G>T. The patient's father (II‐1) did not carry the mutation.

functional.statement: Patient material (proband's muscle biopsy): RT-PCR and sequencing of LAMP2 mRNA showed a 6-nucleotide insertion that introduces a stop codon, predicted to remove the transmembrane domain. No control sample is described; protein was not measured.

quotes.quote: We took a muscle biopsy from the patient, extracted RNA, reverse transcribed it to generate cDNA, and conducted PCR and sequencing analysis.

The results indicated that the identified mutation resulted in the insertion of 6 nucleotides in the mRNA, with the latter three bases forming a stop codon, which resulted in early termination of protein translation and loss of the LAMP2 transmembrane domain (Figure 3).
The mutation did not result in loss of mRNA exons; rather, a 6‐nucleotide (two‐codon) insertion, where the latter was a stop codon, leading to early termination of LAMP2 protein translation.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice-donor change at intron position +1 after c.741 (p.? in the batch); the paper's RNA study reports use of a nearby donor adding 6 nucleotides and a stop codon. The authors link loss of the transmembrane domain to impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion.

quotes.quote: This change will affect the fusion of lysosomes and autophagosomes, and impair the autophagy function of cells, resulting in clinical manifestations.
This alteration led to complete loss of the protein encoded by the transcript after exon 5, including the crucial transmembrane domain.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Annotation databases (in-house cohort, dbSNP138, 1000G) are named in the methods, but no frequency result for this variant is reported.

quotes.quote: SNV data were annotated using data from our in‐house cohort, dbSNP138, and 1000G_OMNI2.5, and the annotated data analyzed using snpEff and deep neural networks developed in‐house.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel pathogenic mutation and state that interpretation followed ACMG guidelines (no criteria listed). PMID 33933120 lists '741 + 1G → T' in a literature table without classification.

quotes.quote: By whole exome sequencing analysis, we identified a novel pathogenic mutation in LAMP2 c.741+1G>T.
Data interpretation was conducted in accordance with the relevant guidelines of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG; Zhou et al., 2018).

concerns: PMID 30714332 contradicts itself on the RNA result: one sentence says 'the latter three bases' of the 6-nt insertion form a stop codon, another says 'the second of which happened to be a stop codon'.

PMID 33933120 (in this batch) lists '741 + 1G → T' under exon 5, Asian, in its literature Table 1 with no person or citation attached; this is probably the same family as PMID 30714332 and should not be counted as a separate case. It was not assigned to this candidate by the batch.
Zygosity is never stated; the paper uses 'carriers' for both the males and the mother.
notes_for_panel: Small family with maternal transmission to two affected sons, father negative, and an RNA study on patient muscle showing aberrant splicing with a premature stop.
